title: Protocol for isolation and proteostatic analysis of sub-populations of spermatogenic cells in mouse
protocol: Prepare three 35-mm dishes, each containing 2 mL DMEM basic media.
Prepare one 35-mm dish containing 2 mL DMEM basic media with 2 mg/mL Collagenase IV and 5 μg/mL DNase I.
Pre-warm all media for 30–60 min in a 37°C humidified incubator with 5% CO2.
Sacrifice four male juvenile mice (10–12-dpp) or one adult mouse (2–3-month) by cervical dislocation after anesthetization with CO2.
Sterilize abdomen using 70% ethanol.
Open abdominal cavity with micro-dissecting scissors and tweezers.
Dissect testes with tweezers and scissors.
Place testes in pre-warmed DMEM basic media.
Remove tunica albuginea from testes.
Dismantle seminiferous tubules and remove attached blood vessels.
Wash seminiferous tubules by moving them through dishes containing clean DMEM basic media.
Transfer cleaned seminiferous tubules to a dish containing media with Collagenase IV and DNase I.
Mince seminiferous tubules into small pieces with a micro-dissecting scissor.
Incubate the dish in the 37°C incubator for 10 min.
Disperse cells once by pipetting up and down gently.
Add 20 μL Trypsin (50 mg/mL stock).
Continue incubation for another 15 min.
Pipet gently to dissociate cells every 5 min.
Clean scissors and tweezers with 70% ethanol between mice during dissection.
Wash seminiferous tubules free of hair before transferring them into enzyme-containing media.
Filter dispersed cells through a 40-μm cell strainer into a 50-mL Corning tube.
Collect cells by centrifugation at 150 × g, 4°C, for 10 min using a refrigerated table-top centrifuge.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cell pellets with 2 mL HBSS.
Count cell numbers with a hemacytometer.
Centrifuge again at 400 × g, 4°C, for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in HBSS containing 5% FBS to a concentration of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Spin down cells.
Resuspend stained cells in 1 mL HBSS containing 5% FBS.
Filter cell suspension through a 40-μm strainer to remove clumps (optional).
Turn on the MoFlo XDP Cell Sorter 30 minutes before running samples.
Adjust sheath stream and laser alignment.
Run 5000–10,000 cells per sample.
Set gate-1 in FSC-Area/SSC-Area to exclude cell debris and aggregates.
Set gate-2 in FSC-Height/FSC-Area to exclude non-single cell clusters.
Apply excitation/emission at 488 nm/507 nm for GFP and 647 nm/780 nm for cKIT.
Set gate-3 using green and red signals on X and Y axis of the contour plot.
Collect sample cells under a fluorescent microscope.
Run all cells using the same gating parameters to sort out GFPHcKIT-, GFPHcKIT+, and GFPLcKIT+ SSCs.
Collect sorted cells into 5-mL Falcon tubes containing 1 mL HBSS.
Centrifuge cells at 700 × g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Proceed to steps 13 or 17–19 for analyses of proteostasis in SSCs.
Alternatively, store cells at −80°C for RNA extraction and quantitative RT-PCR (optional).
Add 1 mL TRIzol reagent into cells before storage to maintain RNA stability (optional).
Make 200 mL 2% and 200 mL 4% BSA in HBSS.
Use 150 mL of each BSA solution to prepare 300 mL 2%-4% consecutive BSA gradient using a gradient mixer.
Fill the plastic pipeline with 2% BSA solutions gently before preparing the gradient to avoid air bubbles.
Autoclave BSA solutions to sterilize for further experimentation.
Disperse testicular cells from 2 adult male mice as described in step 1.
Resuspend cells in 10 mL HBSS, slowly lay cells on top of the BSA gradient.
Stand cells on the BSA gradient for 2.5 h at room temperature.
Manually collect cell fractions into 15-mL Corning tubes, 5 mL/per tube.
Examine spermatocytes, round and elongating spermatids using a light microscope (EVOSfl) according to their cellular morphologies.
Pool fractions containing the same cell types together for further experimentation.
Examine collected fractions under a light microscope to determine which cells are present.
Collect pachytene spermatocytes (SPCY I) with large nuclei and thin cytoplasm rim.
Collect smaller spermatocytes at meiotic II (SPCY II) that follow pachytene spermatocytes in the gradient.
Identify round spermatids by their circular morphology and distinctive dark particle next to the nucleus.
Collect elongating spermatids, characterized by oval-shaped nuclei with hooked tips.
Discard residue bodies shed from maturing sperm if purer fractions of spermatids are required.
Exclude spermatogonial stem cells due to their scarcity in BSA gradient fractionation.
Prepare testicular cell suspensions as described.
Place 1 mL of a single-cell suspension containing 2 × 10^6 cells in a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Add Hoechst 33342 at a concentration of 10 μg/mL to the tube.
Wrap the tube with tinfoil to avoid light exposure.
Incubate the tube in a 32°C water bath for 20 minutes.
Wash cells once with 1 mL HBSS.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL HBSS containing 5% FBS and 2 μg/mL propidium iodide (PI).
Incubate the resuspended cells for 10 minutes.
Wash cells once with 1 mL HBSS.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL HBSS containing 5% FBS.
Turn on LSRFortessa 30 minutes prior to use.
Run 5000–10,000 cells using the instrument.
Set gate-1 in forward scatter area (FSC-A)/side scatter area (SSC-A) to exclude cell debris and aggregates.
Set gate-2 in propidium iodide/FSC-A to exclude PI+ cells.
Set gate-3 in Hoechst Red/Hoechst Blue contour plot to exclude cell debris and clusters for PI- cells.
Run cells using Hoechst Red/ Hoechst Blue channels.
Collect data for further analyses.
Chill 1× PBS on ice.
Transfer 2 × 10^6 dispersed testicular cells (1 mL) into a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge the cells at 400 × g, 4°C, for 5 min.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA), incubate on ice for 30 min.
Wash cells once with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Incubate cells in 1 mL of 1× PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 on ice for 15 min.
Wash cells once more with 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of 1× PBS containing 2% fetal bovine serum (FBS).
Centrifuge the cells to spin down, resuspend cell pellet with 0.5 mL of 1× PBST (1× PBS containing 0.01% Triton X-100).
Add 2.5 μL of PE-conjugated anti-PLZF and 1 μL of eFluor 780-conjugated anti-cKIT to the cell suspension.
Wrap tubes with tin foil, incubate on ice for 60 min.
Wash cells three times with 1 mL 1× PBS on ice for 10 minutes each time.
Spin down cells at 400 × g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 0.5 mL 1× PBST.
Run approximately 5000 cells to select gating parameters as described in step 2g on LSRFortessa.
Apply excitation/emission at 507 nm/561 nm for PLZF and 647 nm/780 nm for cKIT, respectively.
Extract total RNAs from sorted cells using RNAsimple ToTal RNA Kit.
Dissolve RNAs in RNase-free ddH2O.
Determine RNA concentrations via spectrophotometry.
Set up reverse transcription using total RNA from the juvenile mouse in a 0.5-mL Eppendorf tube.
Set up PCR reaction using gene specific primers accordingly.
Use high-fidelity Taq DNA polymerase or equivalent DNA polymerase for the PCR reaction.
Subject PCR products to agarose gel electrophoresis.
Excise gel strips containing the PCR products under UV light.
Purify DNA fragments using TIANgel Midi Purification Kit.
Determine concentrations of purified DNAs using spectrophotometry.
Calculate copy numbers according to molecular weight of DNA: copies/μL = (6.02 × 10²³ copies/mol) × (ng/μL (DNA concentration) × 10⁻⁹)/(bp (DNA length) × 660 gram/mol).
Make 10× dilutions of a series DNA templates as follows: 2 × 10⁷, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 copies/μL.
Set up PCR reactions accordingly.
Run PCR on a CFX96 Real-Time system.
Draw standard curves using DNA copy numbers vs. CT values.
Determine mRNA copy numbers of a specific gene in SSCs using quantitative RT-PCR.
Set up reverse transcription reaction using total RNAs from sorted SSC sub-populations.
Use 1 μL RT samples to run quantitative PCR reactions.
Calculate mRNA copy numbers according to the CT values using the standard curve.
Manipulate RNA-containing samples on a clean bench.
Use RNase-free Eppendorf tubes for sample handling.
Use RNase-free pipette tips during procedures.
Perform immunocytochemistry of spermatocytes undergoing meiotic cell division.
Prepare chromosomal spreads of testicular cells.
Stain cell nuclei with anti-SYCP3 antibody for synaptonemal complex.
Stain cell nuclei with anti-γH2AX antibody for XY chromosomal pairing.
Dissect out testes from adult mice following steps 1a–1d.
Transfer 15-cm long seminiferous tubules into a 35-mm dish containing 1 mL hypotonic solution.
Incubate the tubules in the hypotonic solution at room temperature for 1 hour.
Transfer 3-cm long seminiferous tubules into a 40-μL drop of 100 mM sucrose solution on a glass slide.
Tear the tubule into small pieces with two fine-tipped tweezers.
Pipette up and down to release testicular cells onto the glass slide using a 20-μL pipette-man.
Wet 18 mm × 18 mm cover glass slides by dipping them in fixation buffer.
Transfer a drop of cell suspension (20 μL) onto the upper left corner of a cover slide.
Spread cells first horizontally then vertically by tilting the slide with hand in a swirling motion.
Process the rest of seminiferous tubules following steps c–f.
Dry cover glasses in a moist chamber for 2 hours at room temperature.
Wash cover glasses twice by incubating them in 2 mL 0.4% Photo-Flo 200 solution for 3 minutes each time.
Place cover glasses in 6-well plates.
Block cells with 1 mL 2% BSA/PBST for 2 hours at room temperature.
Remove blocking buffer.
Add 1 mL of 1% BSA/PBST containing anti-SYCP3 (1:400) and anti-γH2AX (1:500).
Incubate overnight at 4°C.
Wash cover glasses three times with 2 mL 1× PBST, for 10 minutes each time the next morning.
Add 1 mL of 1% BSA/PBST containing appropriate fluorescein-tagged secondary antibodies (1:1000).
Incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash cover glasses three times with 2 mL 1× PBST, for 10 minutes each time.
Mount cover glasses onto slides in 50% glycerol/PBST.
Examine slides under a Confocal Laser Scanning Microscope (CLSM).
Take images covering at least 500 spermatocytes.
Dissect out testes from adult mice following steps 1a–1d.
Transfer 6-cm long seminiferous tubules into a 35-mm dish containing 1.5 mL isotonic sodium citrate (2.2%).
Squeeze out spermatogenic cells from seminiferous tubules with tweezers.
Collect cells by centrifuging at 100 × g, room temperature, for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 1.5 mL hypotonic sodium citrate (1%).
Mix and incubate cells at room temperature for 12 minutes.
Centrifuge cells at 100 × g, room temperature, for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 0.5 mL fixation buffer made of 74% ethanol, 25% acetic acid, and 1% chloroform.
Incubate cells at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Repeat the last step once more.
Add 10-μL drop of cell suspensions onto glass slides.
Air dry the slides.
Stain cells with Giemsa diluted in ddH2O (1:20) for 30 min at room temperature.
Wash slides under gently flowing water for 10–20 s.
Air dry the slides.
Check the intensity of Giemsa under a light microscope during washing every 5 s to acquire staining with clear and appropriate intensities.
Seal slides with neutral balsam.
Examine stained cells under a light microscope equipped with a CCD camera.
Take adequate images that include at least 1000 mid-pachytene nuclei.
Count spermatocytes at various stages of the meiotic cell cycle.
From confocal images, count cells with distinct SCYP3 and γH2AX staining patterns to distinguish cells at leptotene, zygotene, pachytene, and diplotene stages.
Calculate percentages of spermatocytes as: Number of spermatocytes at a particular stage/Total number of all spermatocytes counted X 100%.
Count cells with distinct chromosome morphology in defined areas containing 1000 nuclei at the mid-pachytene stage.
Calculate the ratio of MII to MI spermatocytes to reflect the progression from meiosis I to meiosis II.
Distinguish prophase I spermatocytes by examining the appearance of chromosomes stained for SCYP3 and γH2AX in their nuclei.
Identify leptotene spermatocytes by observing a diffused distribution of SCYP3 in nuclei.
Recognize zygotene spermatocytes by noting the formation of thin threads of SCYP3 and the beginning of γH2AX foci.
Determine pachytene spermatocytes by identifying thick strings of SCYP3 and a clear XY body decorated with γH2AX.
Differentiate diplotene spermatocytes by observing SCYP3-positive threads with separated crosses and a γH2AX-positive XY body.
Note MI spermatocytes as cells without nuclear envelopes containing condensed intact homologous chromosomes.
Identify MII spermatocytes as cells without nuclear envelopes containing thinner sister chromatids.
Weigh male mice with a scale.
Inject puromycin (10 mg/mL) intraperitoneally at a dose of 65 mg/kg body weight.
Prepare two 60-mm dishes containing 5 mL 1× PBS.
At 1.5 hours post-injection, sacrifice mice and dissect out testes in 1× PBS.
Wash testes with 1× PBS briefly.
Cut small openings at both ends of testes using a micro-dissecting scissor.
Place testes in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Incubate overnight (12–16 hours) at 4°C.
Poke a few holes on lateral sides of testes with a 30-gauge needle.
Dehydrate fixed testes through a series of ethanol with increasing concentrations: 30%, 50%, 70%, 80%, 90%, 95%, and 100%.
Soak each concentration for 5 minutes.
Embed testes in paraffin.
Cut embedded testes into 5-μm thin sections with a microtome.
Collect sections on glass slides, placing two sections per standard slide.
Bake the slides at 56°C for 10 minutes.
Cool the slides to room temperature and store them at 4°C.
Soak the slides in xylene twice, each for 5 minutes.
Rehydrate the sections by soaking through ethanol solutions: 100% twice for 3 minutes each, 95% once for 3 minutes, and then in PBS twice for 5 minutes each followed by ddH2O once for 2 minutes.
Heat slides with a microwave using medium power for 3 minutes in 0.01 M citrate buffer.
Switch to low power and maintain heating for an additional 20 minutes.
Cool the slides to room temperature and wash them twice in PBS, each for 5 minutes.
Incubate the slides in 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Wash the slides briefly with PBS.
Submerge slides in 2% BSA/PBST for blocking for 2 hours at room temperature.
Remove blocking buffer, dry areas around sections with a paper towel.
Draw hydrophobic circles around tissue sections using a pen.
Add 100 μL of 1% BSA/PBST containing anti-puromycin (diluted 1:1000) to each circle and incubate at 4°C for 2 hours.
Wash the slides three times by submerging them in 2 mL PBST, each for 10 minutes.
Add 100 μL of 1% BSA/PBST containing fluorescein-tagged secondary antibodies (1:1000) to each circle.
Incubate the circles in the dark for 1 hour at room temperature.
Wash slides three times by submerging them in 2 mL of 1× PBST.
Incubate slides in 1× PBST containing 1 μg/mL DAPI (100 μL/circle) in the dark at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Wash slides three times with 1× PBST.
Mount slides in 50% glycerol/PBS.
Examine slides with CLSM.
Count the number of puromycin-positive spermatogenic cells from confocal images.
Measure the intensity of puromycin signals reflecting the quantity of nascent proteins.
Weigh testes following step 12a-iv.
Remove tunica albuginea and wash seminiferous tubules briefly in 1× PBS.
Place washed tubules in a glass homogenizer on ice.
Add ice-cold RIPA buffer containing 1× protease inhibitor cocktail at 100 mg tissue/mL, typically 1 mL for one testis.
Homogenize testes with a glass pestle for 5 minutes on ice.
Transfer the crude homogenates into a 1.5-mL Eppendorf tube and seal it with paraffin film.
Rotate the tube at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge lysates at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer supernatants to fresh Eppendorf tubes.
Measure protein concentration using Enhanced BCA Protein Assay Kit.
Aliquot and store lysates at -80°C.
Mix lysates containing 40 μg proteins with 5× reducing SDS loading buffer at a 4:1 volume ratio.
Boil samples for 5 minutes in a water bath.
Subject samples to denaturing SDS-PAGE (SDS Polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis).
Transfer proteins from polyacrylamide gels to nitrocellulose membrane using semi-dry transfer apparatus at 20 V for 1.5 hours at room temperature.
Block membranes with 5% BSA/TBST at room temperature for 2 hours on a horizontal shaker.
Incubate membranes in 1% BSA/TBST containing primary antibodies (anti-puromycin, 1:10000, anti-α-Tubulin, 1:5000) at 4°C overnight (12–16 h).
Wash membranes three times with 1× TBST by vigorously shaking at room temperature for 10 minutes each.
Incubate membranes in 1% BSA/TBST containing appropriate secondary antibodies (1:5000) at room temperature for 1 hour.
Wash membranes three times with 1× TBST by vigorously shaking at room temperature, 10 minutes each.
Reveal protein bands using an ECL Detection kit.
Image the protein bands with a Chemiluminescence imager.
Analyze intensities of protein bands using ImageJ software.
Incubate 2 × 10^6 cells in DMEM complete media containing 5 μg/mL puromycin for 1 hour in a 37°C humidified incubator, with 5% CO2.
Collect cells into 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes.
Centrifuge the collected cells at 400 × g, 4°C, for 5 minutes.
Wash cells twice with 1× PBS, 5 minutes each.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL of 1× PBS.
Transfer 20 μL of resuspended cells onto poly-lysine coated slides.
Adhere the cells at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Fix cells by dropping 50 μL of 4% PFA on top of adhered cells, incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Remove 4% PFA and add 50 μL of 0.2% Triton X-100 in 1× PBS on top of the cells, incubate at room temperature for 15 minutes to permeabilize cells.
Centrifuge down remaining cells from 13d.
Remove supernatant.
Add 200 μL cell lysis buffer to cells from one testis.
Pipette to mix well and rotate for 30 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge at 12,000 × g, 4°C, for 10 min.
Transfer supernatant to fresh tubes.
Determine protein concentrations using Enhanced BCA Protein Assay Kit.
Aliquot and store lysates at −80°C.
Run SDS-PAGE.
Perform immuno-blotting with anti-puromycin antibody as described in steps 12c-vi–xiv.
Dissect testes from one adult male mouse.
Weigh the dissected testes.
Wash the testes briefly in 1× PBS.
Remove tunica albuginea and blood vessels.
Place seminiferous tubules in a glass homogenizer on ice.
Add ice-cold tissue lysis buffer at a ratio of 1 mL per 100 mg tissue.
Homogenize testes with a glass pestle on ice for 2 min.
Transfer crude lysates to 1.5-mL RNase-free Eppendorf tubes.
Rotate the samples 30 min at 4°C.
Centrifuge the samples at 2,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer supernatants to fresh 15-mL ultracentrifuge tubes and keep on ice.
Centrifuge the samples at 20,000 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer supernatants to 1.5-mL RNase-free Eppendorf tubes and keep on ice.
Resolve pellets from steps d and e in 0.5% SDS.
Sonicate to lyse the samples.
Examine samples using Western blotting along with fractions from sucrose gradient.
Prepare 10% and 50% sucrose solutions with lysis buffer.
Draw borders on tubes using the Marker block for dividing 13-mL ultracentrifuge tubes into heavy and light sucrose fractions.
Add 10% sucrose from the bottom of the tube to the high sucrose line using the low sucrose loading pipette.
Insert high sucrose loading pipette to the bottom of the tube, add 50% sucrose until it reaches the high sucrose line.
Push 10% sucrose upward to the low sucrose line.
Close the tube with the Stopper gently at a tilted angle to drive air bubbles out through the air hole.
Turn on the Gradient Master 108.
Level the magnetic platform with a Bubble Level.
Select appropriate time, angle, and speed according to the provided index table.
Place sucrose tubes on the tube holder.
Start the run.
Use time/angle/speed of 0.05/87/30 for SW41 rotor to make 10%–50% gradient.
Stand sucrose gradients on ice.
Layer 0.5 mL testes lysates on top of the sucrose gradient.
Balance tubes with lysis buffer by weighing on a Balancer.
Turn on the Optima L-80 XP Ultracentrifuge 30 min prior to run.
Cool the ultracentrifuge and rotor to 4°C.
Place sucrose gradients in SW41 rotor.
Centrifuge at 210,000 × g, 4°C, for 2 h with fastest acceleration and slowest deceleration speed.
Carefully take out tubes without disturbing the gradients.
Collect 0.5-mL fractions into RNase-free Eppendorf tubes using the BioComp Fractionator.
Clean tubing on the fractionator with DEPC-ddH2O before and after collecting fractions.
Take fractions from top to bottom.
Monitor and record OD260 simultaneously.
Draw curves of OD260 for ribosome profiles.
Measure protein concentrations of fractions using Enhanced BCA Protein Assay Kit.
Examine proteins contained in fractions by SDS-PAGE and Western blotting.
Extract RNAs contained in fractions using RNAsimple ToTal RNA Kit.
Generate cDNA library from extracted RNAs using reverse transcription and PCR if required for RNA sequencing.
Store fractions at −80°C if not used immediately.
Prepare testes lysates according to the protocol.
Perform SDS-PAGE using the prepared testes lysates.
Conduct immuno-blotting using antibodies against DNAJB6 at a concentration of 1:2000.
Conduct immuno-blotting using antibodies against DNAJB8 at a concentration of 1:2000.
Conduct immuno-blotting using antibodies against Ubiquitin at a concentration of 1:1000.
Compare the relative quantities of proteins using ImageJ software.
Prepare testes sections as described in steps 12a-iv to viii.
Perform immuno-staining with antibodies against DNAJB6 (1:100) and DNAJB8 (1:100).
Examine stained sections with CLSM.
Weigh testes extracted from adult mice.
Remove tunica albuginea and attached blood vessels in 60-mm dishes containing 1× PBS.
Dismantle seminiferous tubules, wash through fresh 1× PBS.
Transfer seminiferous tubules to a glass homogenizer pre-chilled on ice.
Add lysis buffer at a ratio of 1 mL per testis.
Homogenize briefly with a glass pestle.
Transfer the crude lysates to 1.5-mL Eppendorf tubes.
Rotate the tubes for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Spin the samples at 6,000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer supernatants to fresh tubes.
Dilute 20× Detection Reagent to 1× with 1× assay buffer provided in the Proteostat Protein Aggregation Assay Kit.
Mix 98 μL of testis lysate with 2 μL of 1× Detection Reagent.
Add the mixture to a 96-well plate, one mix per well.
Incubate for 15 min in the dark at room temperature.
Read fluorescent signals on a multimode microplate reader using excitation and emission wavelengths of 550 nm and 600 nm, respectively.
